findings.claim: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the result of getResourceTypeResource() can be null and is passed to findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. This causes a NullPointerException, which surfaces as HTTP 500 instead of 403. It can also happen when realm admin permissions are disabled after the client exists.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:217-219 passes the result of getResourceTypeResource() straight to findByResource() without a null check. getResourceTypeResource() returns null when realm admin permissions are off (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:117-118, 144-149), and both findByResource implementations then call resource.getId() (JPAPolicyStore.java:215, StoreFactoryCacheSession.java:938). Turning admin permissions off only clears the realm flag (DefaultExportImportManager.java:783) and leaves the permissions client in place, so realmResourceServer() is still non-null and this code is reached.

findings.claim: The AdminPermissions role/client/group removal listener is guarded only by the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, the permission cleanup block is skipped and permission resources are left orphaned.

verifier.reason: The patch wraps the role/client/group removal listener in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` (AdminPermissions.java:77). V1 and V2 are versions of the same feature and cannot both be on (Profile.java:56-58), so under V2 the block never runs. Nothing else deletes V2 resources: AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104 owns them by the admin-permissions client, and ClientApplicationSynchronizer.java:49-75 only removes the deleted client's own resource server and client policies, so the V2 'Clients' resource for a deleted client is left behind.

findings.claim: The removal listener is now wrapped in a V1-only feature gate. Deployments without V1 no longer clean up leftover V1 permission resources and policies when a role, client or group is deleted.

verifier.reason: Before the patch, deployments without V1 never cleaned up V1 leftovers either. With no fine-grained feature enabled, `authz` is null (MgmtPermissions.java:85-88), so `realmResourceServer()` returns null (MgmtPermissions.java:251) and `deletePermissions` exits early (ClientPermissions.java:189-190). With V2 enabled, `getRealmPermissionsClient()` points at the V2 admin-permissions client, not realm-management (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:52-53), and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws an exception; the new gate at AdminPermissions.java:77 avoids that throw.

findings.claim: Under V2, deleting a client leaves its per-client resource and scope permissions orphaned, because there is no V2 cleanup path.

verifier.reason: In V2, a per-client resource is created by getOrCreateResource (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104). It is named after the client's id but owned by the admin-permissions client. When a client is deleted, nothing removes it: AdminPermissions' ClientRemovedEvent listener is gated on V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (patch line 76), and ClientApplicationSynchronizer.java:49-75 only removes the deleted client's own resource server and its entries in client policies. So the resource and its scope permissions are left behind.

findings.claim: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission uses findByType(server, 'Clients'). This matches only the typed all-clients resource, because per-client resources are created without a type. As a result it never returns per-client IDs and may return the string 'Clients', which callers such as AvailableRoleMappingResource pass to realm.getClientById.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 calls findByType(server, "Clients") and adds resource.getName(). Per-client resources are created at AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104 with no setType, so they never match. Only the all-clients resource gets a type (setType at AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250), so the method never returns per-client IDs and can return the name "Clients". AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:230 then calls realm.getClientById("Clients").getRolesStream(), and since no client has that ID this would throw a NullPointerException.

findings.claim: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) looks up the resource with findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()). AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with owner resourceServer.getClientId(), so the lookup never finds them and always falls back to the all-clients resource.

verifier.reason: ResourceServer.getClientId() just returns getId() in both the JPA adapter (model/jpa/.../ResourceServerAdapter.java:91-93) and the Infinispan adapter (ResourceServerAdapter.java:121-123). So the owner set at AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104 is server.getId(), and the resource name is client.getId() (via resolveClient). The lookup findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) in the patch's hasPermission matches the per-client resource and does not fall back to the all-clients resource.

findings.claim: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) does not filter on permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.java:135.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), added at change.patch lines 493-521, goes through every evaluated Permission and returns true on any matching scope without checking permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()). UserPermissionsV2.java:135 does make that check. The hasGrantedPermission helper (change.patch lines 560-572) also leaves it out.

findings.claim: ClientPermissionsV2 uses Arrays.asList() for single-element lists where List.of() could be used.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:225 and :250 (both new in this patch) build a one-element list with `List<String> expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope);`. Each list is only used for a `contains` check, so `List.of(scope)` or a plain `scope.equals(s)` would work just as well.

findings.claim: An empty line was replaced by a line containing four spaces of trailing whitespace.

verifier.reason: The patch removes the empty line after the class declaration in server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java and adds one that holds only four spaces. That whitespace-only line is now at line 53 of the file.

findings.claim: There is no migration for realms whose admin-permissions client already existed. Those realms never receive the Clients resource type or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). As a result getResourceTypeResource returns null, and creating a Clients permission fails with 'Scope [configure] does not exist' or 'No scopes found'.

verifier.reason: AdminPermissionsSchema.init (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:222-228) returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, and it is the only place that creates scopes and type resources (lines 237-254). No migration in model/storage-private/.../migration touches AdminPermissionsSchema. So existing realms never get the Clients resource or the configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes: getResourceTypeResource returns null (line 133), getScope throws 'Scope [configure] does not exist.' (line 210), and getOrCreateResource throws 'No scopes found.' (line 108).

findings.claim: Tests access getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) without checking that the list has at least two elements, which risks an IndexOutOfBoundsException.

verifier.reason: In PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient (change.patch:862-865), the test only asserts `not(empty())` and then calls `defaultClientScopes.get(1)`, so nothing checks that the list has two elements. Line 839 also calls `.get(1)` inside a try block that expects ForbiddenException. In practice a realm's built-in default scopes (profile, email, roles, web-origins and others) make the list long enough, so the risk is small.

findings.claim: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. When token-exchange and admin-fine-grained-authz:v2 are both enabled, this produces HTTP 500 instead of 403.

verifier.reason: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 on, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns the new ClientPermissionsV2. Its canExchangeTo(client, to, token) always throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276 calls it with no try/catch, so token exchange to another client's audience fails with HTTP 500 instead of the 403 at line 280.

findings.claim: The evaluate-and-match-scope loop is duplicated three times: hasGrantedPermission duplicates ClientPermissions.hasPermission(Resource,String), and the two hasPermission overloads repeat the same logic.

verifier.reason: In ClientPermissionsV2.java (new file, patch lines 493-572), hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String) is a line-for-line copy of the private ClientPermissions.hasPermission(Resource,String) at ClientPermissions.java:689-701. Both hasPermission(ClientModel,String) and hasPermission(String) repeat the same evaluatePermission call and nested scope-matching loop, with only the resource lookup differing.

findings.claim: The label 'area/dependencies' does not exist for Dependabot to use.

verifier.reason: The patch only changes Java permission and test files and does not touch Dependabot config. The 'area/dependencies' label used in .github/dependabot.yml:12,23 also appears in .github/teams.yml:55, so the repository does define it.

findings.claim: The label 'area/ci' does not exist for Dependabot to use.

verifier.reason: The patch only changes Java permission classes and tests, and never touches Dependabot config. The 'area/ci' label is already used in .github/dependabot.yml:13 and .github/teams.yml:7, which suggests it exists; whether it is defined on GitHub cannot be checked from the source.

findings.claim: Once a per-client permission exists for a client, all-clients permissions stop applying to it. Per-client resources are created without a type, and DefaultPolicyEvaluator adds type-level policies only when resource.getType() != null.

verifier.reason: AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104 creates the per-client resource with no type, and an all-clients permission is attached only to the typed 'Clients' resource (AuthorizationProvider.java:323-326). Once a per-client resource exists, ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(client, scope) (patch lines ~500-510) evaluates only that resource, and DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:73 skips type-level policies when getType() is null, so all-clients grants are ignored for canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles on that client.

findings.claim: Tests are missing for MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, the client-scope endpoints, realm-management escalation, and V2 delete cleanup.

verifier.reason: The patch adds V2 checks for MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE (ClientPermissionsV2.java canMapClientScopeRoles, patch ~L387) and for realm-level client scopes (canManageClientScopes and canView(ClientScopeModel), ~L392-408), but no test in tests/base/.../fgap uses MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, the client-scopes endpoints, or realm-management escalation. PermissionClientTest.java only calls per-client getDefaultClientScopes/add/remove (lines ~148-230), and testManageAllClients deletes a client without checking that its V2 permission resources get cleaned up.

findings.claim: The Javadoc on the void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says 'Returns true if...', but these methods throw ForbiddenException and return nothing.

verifier.reason: In ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:95-103, the patch adds Javadoc reading 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}' (and the same for canViewClientScopes) to the methods `void requireView()` and `void requireViewClientScopes()`. Both methods are void, so they cannot return true; they are require-style checks that throw when access is denied.

findings.claim: The new feature gate re-indents the listener body and changes cast spacing from (X)event to (X) event, which are formatting changes unrelated to the fix.

verifier.reason: In AdminPermissions.java (patch lines 76-95), the listener body is wrapped in a new `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check, and every cast changes from `(X)event` to `(X) event`, e.g. `(RoleContainerModel.RoleRemovedEvent) event` and `((ClientModel) role.getContainer())`. The re-indent follows from adding the wrapper, but the cast spacing changes no behaviour and only adds diff noise.

findings.claim: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName has no CLIENTS case and handles only Users, so Clients resources resolve to a null display name.

verifier.reason: In AdminPermissionsSchema.java:304-326, getResourceName only checks the Users type (line 310). Clients resources fall through to resource.getDisplayName() (line 325), which is never set: they are created with only a name (line 104), so PolicyResourceService.java:218 returns a null displayName for them.

findings.claim: The Javadoc text 'For V2 only: Also if ... for all clients' misdescribes V2 behavior: V2 replaces the V1 per-client check rather than adding to it, and V2 also honours per-client grants.

verifier.reason: The Javadoc lists the role check, the per-client permission and then, for V2, the extra all-clients permission. ClientPermissionsV2.java:64-69/91-103 does exactly that: role, or hasPermission(client, scope), which checks the per-client resource and falls back to the all-clients resource (lines 214-222). V2 does override the V1 code, but it keeps the per-client semantics the doc describes, so the 'Also ... for all clients' wording is accurate rather than misleading.

findings.claim: ClientPermissionsV2 contains dead code copied from V1 token-exchange support: the private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method, the logger field, the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, and the Scope, ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext and EvaluationContext imports are all unused.

verifier.reason: In the new file ClientPermissionsV2.java, the private getEvaluationContext at :262-272 is never called, the logger at :51 and the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import at :46 are never used, and the Scope import at :27 is never referenced. The ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext and EvaluationContext imports (:22,:23,:29) are used only inside that dead method, so in practice they are dead too.

findings.claim: A new private ClientPermissionsV2 clientPermissions field hides the inherited protected clientPermissions field from MgmtPermissions.

verifier.reason: MgmtPermissionsV2.java:29 declares `private ClientPermissionsV2 clientPermissions`, which hides `protected ClientPermissions clientPermissions` at MgmtPermissions.java:76. It does no harm, because the base field is only touched inside the overridden clients() (MgmtPermissions.java:222-224), and the patch follows the existing userPermissions pattern (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:27).

findings.claim: testViewAllClients calls create(null) and never tests a real payload.

verifier.reason: In the patch's testViewAllClients, the 'can't create a new client' check calls clients().create(null) (change.patch:1011) and no create call in that test sends a real ClientRepresentation. The 403 assertion is still meaningful because ClientsResource.createClient checks auth.clients().requireManage() before it reads the body (ClientsResource.java:186).

findings.claim: An all-clients map-roles grant, or configure plus map-roles-composite, also covers the realm-management client. This lets an admin with map-roles on users grant realm-admin privileges, bypassing checkAdminRoles validation.

verifier.reason: Under V2, ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission (patch lines 493-508) falls back to the all-clients resource whenever a client has no resource of its own, so canMapRoles and canMapCompositeRoles also return true for the realm-management client. RolePermissions.canMapRole (RolePermissions.java:307-308) and canMapComposite (RolePermissions.java:397-398) return true straight away in that case, without calling checkAdminRoles (lines 149-287), so an admin holding that grant can map admin roles such as realm-admin.

findings.claim: canView() accepts only the VIEW scope and not MANAGE, so GET /client-scopes returns 403 for admins with only all-clients MANAGE. This is inconsistent with canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel).

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() (patch line 372-374) returns canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW) and never checks MANAGE, while canView(ClientScopeModel) (line 404-408) accepts VIEW or MANAGE and canManageClientScopes() (line 392-396) accepts MANAGE. GET /client-scopes calls requireListClientScopes() (ClientScopesResource.java:91), which checks canView() || QUERY_CLIENTS (ClientPermissions.java:258-260), so an admin with only all-clients MANAGE gets 403; MgmtPermissions.evaluatePermission does not treat manage as implying view.

findings.claim: The tests do not clean up after themselves: @AfterEach removes only permissions, testManageOnlyOneClient leaves a renamed client and changed client-scope types, and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient leaves roles and mappings behind. Results therefore depend on test order.

verifier.reason: The @AfterEach in PermissionClientTest (patch lines 792-797) removes only scope permissions, and ManagedRealm.runCleanup (test-framework/.../ManagedRealm.java:66-72) runs only registered cleanup tasks, so the realm, which is shared by the class (InjectRealm lifecycle CLASS), keeps the leftovers. testManageOnlyOneClient renames myclient and moves a default scope to optional (patch 857-869), and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient creates roles, a user mapping and a composite (patch 1022-1055), with no cleanup. However, I found no existing assertion in this class that changes with test order, so the order dependence is a risk, not a failure that happens today.

findings.claim: The test imports the JUnit 4 org.junit.Assert.fail while the rest of the file uses JUnit 5 Assertions.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `import static org.junit.Assert.fail;` (JUnit 4) at PermissionClientTest.java:25. The same file also uses `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions` (JUnit 5, line 40) for `Assertions.assertEquals` (lines 259, 313, 321) and the JUnit 5 `@Test`/`@AfterEach` annotations.

findings.claim: The createClientPolicy method is never used.

verifier.reason: The patch adds the protected static helper createClientPolicy(ManagedRealm, ManagedClient, String, String) at tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/AbstractPermissionTest.java:136, and a repo-wide search finds no call to it. The only other createClientPolicy matches are a different private method in UMAPolicyProviderFactory.java:406.

findings.claim: No documentation is added for the Clients resource type or its scopes.

verifier.reason: The patch only touches Java sources and tests. It adds CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and the configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes in AdminPermissionsSchema.java:12-25 without Javadoc, and it changes no .adoc file under docs/. The existing Users resource type for fine-grained admin permissions v2 has no docs in the repo either.

findings.claim: hasPermission(String) runs a full policy evaluation of the all-clients resource on every call without checking whether any policies exist, causing repeated evaluations per client in GET /clients.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String) (patch lines 523-546) checks only that the 'Clients' resource exists, and the schema always creates it (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:247). It then calls root.evaluatePermission, which has no cache (MgmtPermissions.java:347-351), and unlike hasPermission(ClientModel,String) it never checks findByResource for policies. ClientsResource.java:148/151 calls canView(c) per client, which calls canView() and so hasPermission(VIEW) again, up to twice per client.

findings.claim: hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) duplicates canManageClientsDefault(), and hasOneAdminRole(VIEW_CLIENTS, MANAGE_CLIENTS) duplicates canViewClientDefault().

verifier.reason: ClientPermissions.java:268-273 defines canManageClientsDefault() as root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) and canViewClientDefault() as root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS, VIEW_CLIENTS). The new ClientPermissionsV2 makes these same calls inline (patch lines 352, 393, 405) instead of using the helpers, even though it calls canViewClientDefault() at line 373.
